title: The Clean Air Lab
story: You and NOVA are at the city's environment lab when the air-lock doors seal. NOVA is preparing a report on pollution. It must use data honestly and get its facts right before the doors open.
escaped: The air-lock opens. NOVA now treats patterns with care, sorts waste correctly and checks claims about drinking water.

locks.title: Cars and coughs
locks.intro: NOVA found city data for ten years.
locks.question: NOVA concludes: 'Asthma makes people buy more cars.' What is the honest conclusion?
options: NOVA is right: the numbers rise together.
More likely the other way: more cars, more smoke, more breathing problems. But rising together isn't proof alone, so check other pollution sources too.
Cars and asthma have nothing to do with air.
Ten years of data proves everything beyond doubt.
locks.hint: Both numbers rise together. Which way round makes sense, and could anything else also play a part?
locks.learn: Two numbers rising together (correlation) doesn't show which causes which, or that there's no third cause. Science (vehicle smoke harms breathing) helps choose the sensible explanation.

locks.title: Will it rot away?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort waste into biodegradable (broken down by microorganisms) and non-biodegradable. Choose its clues.
locks.hint: A wooden toy is hard; a polythene sheet is soft. What decides whether microorganisms can break it down?
locks.learn: Softness and where waste comes from are surface details. Microorganisms break down things that came from plants or animals, so that is the clue that works.

locks.title: Check NOVA's water advice
locks.intro: NOVA is advising a village about drinking water. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: If water looks clear, it is safe to drink.
evidence: Water can look clear and still carry disease-causing microorganisms; boiling or chlorination makes it safe to drink.
Water is filtered through layers of sand and gravel.
The Ganga Action Plan began in 1985.
Some factories release waste into rivers.
locks.hint: Can you see microorganisms with your eyes?
locks.learn: Judging by looks is risky for people and for AI. Microorganisms are invisible, so the evidence must come from tests and treatment, not appearance.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's pollutant facts
locks.intro: NOVA has notes on air pollutants. Tick the notes that are wrong.

rows.label: Reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen
Makes the ozone layer thicker
rows.why: carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat

rows.label: Main cause of the greenhouse effect
rows.why: greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide cause it

locks.hint: Which gases trap heat in the greenhouse effect? Which harms the ozone layer?
locks.learn: A report built on wrong facts would push the wrong solutions. Checking the training data is the first step to an AI you can trust.
